         1                 P R O C E E D I N G S

         2                  ACTING PRESIDENT BRESLIN:    The

         3       Senate will please come to order.

         4                  I ask all to rise and repeat with

         5       me the Pledge of Allegiance.

         6                  (Whereupon, the assemblage recited

         7       the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.)

         8                  ACTING PRESIDENT BRESLIN:    In the

         9       absence of clergy, may we bow our heads for a

        10       moment of silence.

        11                  (Whereupon, the assemblage

        12       respected a moment of silence.)

        13                  ACTING PRESIDENT BRESLIN:

        14       Senator Smith.

        15                  SENATOR SMITH:    Yes,

        16       Mr. President.  It is my understanding that

        17       the Governor has issued a proclamation that

        18       seeks to convene the legislative extraordinary

        19       session.

        20                  ACTING PRESIDENT BRESLIN:    Yes,

        21       Senator Smith, we have received such a message

        22       from the Governor.

        23                  SENATOR SMITH:    Mr. President, as

        24       you and my colleagues will recall, the

        25       Governor convened this Senate into



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                                         6954



         1       extraordinary session on January 18th, and we

         2       have remained in such an extraordinary session

         3       without adjourning sine die.

         4                  Therefore, I would suggest that the

         5       proclamation is not valid, as it asserts

         6       powers that the Governor does not

         7       constitutionally possess.

         8                  ACTING PRESIDENT BRESLIN:

         9       Senator Smith, your point is well taken.

        10       Inasmuch as the Senate remains in

        11       extraordinary session, the Governor cannot

        12       convene this house into an additional

        13       extraordinary session.

        14                  The Governor does have the power,

        15       however, to recommend additional subject

        16       matters beyond those he enumerated in his

        17       initial proclamation.

        18                  I am therefore willing that the

        19       communication from the Governor that is

        20       currently before the house be deemed a message

        21       recommending additional subject matter to be

        22       considered as part of the extraordinary

        23       session convened on January 18, 2010.

        24                  The Secretary will read the message

        25       from the Governor.



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                                         6955



         1                  THE SECRETARY:    "Pursuant to the

         2       power vested in me by Article IV, Section 3 of

         3       the Constitution, I hereby convene the Senate

         4       and the Assembly of the State of New York in

         5       Extraordinary Session, at the Capitol, in the

         6       City of Albany, on the twenty-seventh day of

         7       June, two thousand ten, at seven o'clock p.m.,

         8       for the purpose of considering legislation I

         9       will submit with respect to various items, and

        10       for the consideration of legislation with

        11       respect to such other subjects as I may

        12       recommend.

        13                  "Given under my hand and the Privy

        14       Seal of the State in the City of Albany this

        15       twenty-sixth day of June in the year two

        16       thousand ten, David A. Paterson, Governor."

        17                  ACTING PRESIDENT BRESLIN:

        18       Senator Smith.

        19                  SENATOR SMITH:    Mr. President, is

        20       there any further business at the desk?

        21                  ACTING PRESIDENT BRESLIN:

        22       Senator Smith, the desk is clear.

        23                  SENATOR SMITH:    There being no

        24       further business at the desk, I move that we

        25       adjourn at the call of the Temporary



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.

         1       President.

         2                  ACTING PRESIDENT BRESLIN:    There

         3       being no further business, the Senate will

         4       stand in recess at the call of the Temporary

         5       President.

         6                  (Whereupon, at 7:10 p.m., the

         7       Senate adjourned.)
